frames.narration: Orders are appended to the event log as they happen. Both jobs will count orders per 10-minute window of event time. Window 10:00 to 10:10 has 100 on-time orders so far.
The stream job reads the log continuously and keeps a running count per window in state. Its watermark is the newest event time minus a 30 second wait.
At 10:10:30 the watermark reaches 10:10:00, so the stream emits the window: 100 orders, about 30 seconds after it closed.
A phone was offline: an order from 10:09:55 only reaches the log at 10:11:30. The stream already emitted that window, so it drops the event as late.
The result table still says 100, which is wrong by 1. A longer watermark wait would have caught it, but every answer would then arrive more than 90 seconds late.
Hours later the batch job runs over the bounded slice of the log that holds the whole window. It sees all 101 orders, including the late one.
The batch overwrites the row by key (10:00), so a re-run gives the same table instead of double counting. Finance now has the exact 101; the dashboard was fast, the batch was right.
